nodes.label: The leakage and invariant suite (86 -> 101 gates)
nodes.norm_label: the leakage and invariant suite (86 -> 101 gates)
nodes.rationale: Gates the build: packaging writes nothing if any gate fails, on the principle that a dataset with a leak, once written, is a dataset somebody will train on. The count of gates is not a measure of their coverage - 83 gates passed a build in which 36 per cent of the Ebola target was fabricated and 31 per cent of dengue's observed cells sat in mixed-phase columns; both defects were found in adversarial review, not by the suite. A green suite is evidence only about the properties it actually tests.

nodes.label: build_datasets.py - verify, construct, gate, write
nodes.rationale: The step order is deliberate. Verification halts the build rather than warning, because a drifted input would change every reported figure while the datasets still passed their own schema checks. The leakage gates run before packaging because a dataset containing a leak, once written to disk, is a dataset somebody will train on.

nodes.label: loaders/covid_load.py - the one fetched source
nodes.rationale: COVID is fetched from the NYT repository's master branch, a reference that can move by construction, which is exactly why it is pinned. A downloaded source is more exposed to drift than a placed one, not less, so exempting it from the pin would have been backwards. 'Archived upstream' is a reason to expect stability, not a substitute for checking it.

nodes.label: Encoder test gates, each with a paired negative control
nodes.norm_label: encoder test gates, each with a paired negative control
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the Phase-2 discipline: a gate that cannot fail proves nothing. Covers no node-indexed params, size agnosticism, isolated-node finiteness, no covariates, masked loss, per-origin scaler refit, permutation equivariance, no rollout, gate-nests-graph-free, receptive field, and normalisation round-trip - each with a planted defect the gate must catch.

nodes.label: test_schema.py shape and invariant contracts
nodes.rationale: Covers the tricky invariants, not just shapes: cumulative->incidence envelope and mask, leakage-safe train scaler, few-shot support with disjoint query and pooled scaler, obs_mask core channel, transfer_view core-only, accent-stripped joins, multi-country coverage prune.

nodes.label: to_schema.py (loaders, graph builders, scalers, splits)
nodes.rationale: fit_scalers* and apply_scaler are deliberately separate steps: raw counts are assembled, the fit set is chosen, and only then are stats computed, so leakage cannot happen by accident.

nodes.label: Calendar-causality gate for the few-shot split
nodes.norm_label: calendar-causality gate for the few-shot split
nodes.rationale: Checks that every support cell is dated on or before every query cell, computed from the cells' dates rather than from the mask that defines them - the property the earlier suite structurally could not test. It cannot be probed by perturbing week zero: the series is cumulative, so altering the initial value also alters the week-one increment and the test would fail for the wrong reason; the perturbation must be applied to a query week.

nodes.label: Determinism verified, not assumed
nodes.rationale: Node and date order are the schema's single source of truth and are fixed by the loaders; two consecutive builds produce identical arrays for all datasets.

nodes.label: Six negative controls that plant real defects
nodes.norm_label: six negative controls that plant real defects
nodes.rationale: A gate that cannot fail establishes nothing. Each control plants a defect and requires the corresponding gate to fail: a development scaler fitted on all cells; the Ebola scaler fitted on support and query; the target planted in an input channel; weekly incidence inflated past its cumulative reference; a training cell placed inside a test column; and a support cell dated after a query cell.

nodes.label: Checksum-pinned public provenance for every raw input
nodes.norm_label: checksum-pinned public provenance for every raw input
nodes.rationale: Every raw input is publicly downloadable and verified before use, so the datasets reproduce end to end from published sources. Versioning differs by source: OpenDengue and GADM are frozen citable releases, the influenza matrices are a vendored benchmark verified against an independent mirror, and the Ebola compilation has no version number at all - its checksum is its only version identifier.

nodes.label: Two build environments (base vs conda ebola)
nodes.norm_label: two build environments (base vs conda ebola)
nodes.rationale: Schema unit tests carry no geospatial dependencies and run in seconds; the fixtures are plain text precisely so that this stays true. Everything touching geometry runs in the pinned conda environment.

nodes.label: Three environments, and the ebola-train split
nodes.norm_label: three environments, and the ebola-train split
nodes.rationale: The training code reads .npz and needs numpy + torch only - it never touches geometry - so forcing torch and the GEOS/GDAL/PROJ stack to co-resolve in one conda environment is a solved problem turned into an afternoon. scipy earns its place for the significance battery and nothing else; do not add a statistics framework for two tests. Hardware is an RTX 3060 with 12 GB, not the 8 GB the Phase-2 guide stated.

nodes.label: Scaler gates built as probes, after a circularity failure
nodes.norm_label: scaler gates built as probes, after a circularity failure
nodes.rationale: A cell the scaler must not see is corrupted, the scaler refitted, and the gate requires that nothing moves. The first suite recovered raw counts by inverting the normalised series with the very scaler under test - circular, because the reconstruction already carries the leak - and it passed a deliberately leaked Ebola scaler with every gate green. Each dataset therefore now ships its raw, unscaled incidence, which no scaler has touched, and every scaler gate is evaluated against that.

nodes.label: Compressed array archive, not a serialised Python object
nodes.norm_label: compressed array archive, not a serialised python object
nodes.rationale: A pickle couples the file to the exact class definitions and library versions that wrote it, so renaming a field or upgrading a library renders it unreadable, and deserialising it executes code, which makes it unsafe to hand to a reviewer.

nodes.label: What permutation equivariance does and does not prove
nodes.norm_label: what permutation equivariance does and does not prove
nodes.rationale: It proves node-order independence, not disease-agnosticism. The encoder can still infer which pathogen it is looking at from N, graph density, seasonal amplitude and mask sparsity, none of which any test removes. The defensible claim is narrower and exactly two things - no static covariate reaches the trunk, and no parameter is node-indexed - which is disease-agnosticism at the parameterisation level, not the information level. Concede it explicitly, or a reviewer will write 'the model can identify the pathogen from dynamics alone' and be right.

nodes.label: Phase-3 data-code freeze and the escalation rule
nodes.norm_label: phase-3 data-code freeze and the escalation rule
nodes.rationale: to_schema.py, build_datasets.py and the leakage suite are frozen. Every number in data_audit.md is computed from these files and the manuscript quotes them, so if a bundle looks wrong that is an escalation, not a patch. The processed .npz files are read-only inputs: row i is meta['node_ids'][i] and column t is meta['dates'][t], and nothing downstream re-derives that correspondence.

nodes.label: Every Day-12 assertion ships with a negative control
nodes.norm_label: every day-12 assertion ships with a negative control
nodes.rationale: A gate that cannot fail proves nothing - the Phase-2 discipline carried forward. Each assertion is paired with a planted defect that requires the assertion to fire: no NaN in A-hat, the trunk rejecting C with a TypeError, LTR reusing the degree vector, RF >= 20, g=0 reproducing the temporal-only model, and no shared-trunk parameter with a dimension in {10, 47, 49, 61, 7165}.

nodes.label: covid_split_probe.py (Test 2: A Better Split)
nodes.rationale: Moves Omicron into train and excludes no data; rejected because the model-over-best-floor ratio is worse at three of four horizons and seed sd triples to 29-38%, which alone disqualifies it for a reported number.

nodes.label: covid_val_probe.py (Test 1: Model Selection)
nodes.rationale: Three arms, one variable each, with arm A reproducing the on-disk records seed-for-seed as a harness self-check; cleaning the selection fold recovers 13-49%, but the excision rule peeks at test to design the protocol so it cannot ship.

nodes.label: E2: Few-Shot Beats Zero-Shot at h3 and h5
nodes.norm_label: e2: few-shot beats zero-shot at h3 and h5
nodes.rationale: Moderate confidence; the weakest thing the adapter has to do and where it has the most examples.

nodes.label: E4: h15 Head Block Must Be a Uniform Shrink of Its Initialisation
nodes.norm_label: e4: h15 head block must be a uniform shrink of its initialisation
nodes.rationale: Not a prediction but a consequence of zero h15 adaptation pairs: the mask zeroes the h15 pinball term so Adam's update is exactly zero and only AdamW's decoupled weight decay moves the block. Any departure from proportionality means a label-driven gradient reached a horizon with no labels, a bug not a result.

nodes.label: Few-Shot FiLM Adapter (1,428 params)
nodes.rationale: Frozen trunk plus one fresh FiLM-plus-quantile-head adapter fit on that arm's support cells only.

nodes.label: All-Dev-Bundle Joint Trunk
nodes.rationale: One shared encoder on all five dev bundles with adapter_groups=[0,1,1,1,2] so each disease gets one adaptation surface; 5 seeds, 91,000 steps, trunk_patience=30 against LDO3's 12 because the cosine schedule is scaled to a budget early stopping never reaches.

nodes.label: encoder_mc Bias Correction
nodes.rationale: Fitted on the validation fold, so on the shipped split it makes COVID worse at every horizon by 8.8 to 47.3 per cent; with the selection fold cleaned it becomes the better arm, so one change repaired two mechanisms that read the same fold.

nodes.label: Omicron as a 6x Structural Break
nodes.rationale: 5.1 million national weekly cases at week 102, the largest value in a 164-week series, sitting at 62% through it; the panel breaks the stationarity assumption the whole protocol rests on in five separate places at once.

nodes.label: Pre-Registration Amendment Log
nodes.rationale: Every change with its reason, all predating the first Ebola score; nothing may be added once scoring has run.

nodes.label: Why the COVID Single-Disease Encoder Has No Skill
nodes.norm_label: why the covid single-disease encoder has no skill
nodes.rationale: Diagnosis complete, two candidate fixes tested end to end and one rejected; no bundle rebuilt and no canonical record overwritten.

nodes.label: Leave-One-District-Out Adapter Stopping Rule (A2)
nodes.rationale: Ebola has no validation split by construction, so epoch count would otherwise be a free parameter chosen after seeing the answer; LODO CV inside the support set reads no query cell.

nodes.label: Zero Left-Pad for Short Windows (A3)
nodes.rationale: window_slice refused t<19 so no adaptation origin could be built; zero equals the per-node mean in normalised space, but sin_doy/cos_doy are zeroed too, which is not a point on the unit circle, so a padded step carries an impossible calendar date.

nodes.label: Add COVID-19 Back as a Third Development Disease
nodes.norm_label: add covid-19 back as a third development disease
nodes.rationale: Restructured folds make the claim honest and a third disease makes it strong.

nodes.label: Untested Option: Use the Deaths Column
nodes.norm_label: untested option: use the deaths column
nodes.rationale: Already in the source file, so it needs no new acquisition and keeps the identical graph and node set; Omicron was enormous in cases and far smaller in deaths, so the 6x break may largely disappear. A hypothesis, not a result.

nodes.label: Omicron Has No Good Home
nodes.rationale: In val, selection and the bias correction target a regime absent from test; in train, the model learns 5M-scale excursions and emits them on a flat tail; in test, it is an unprecedented 3.8x event to extrapolate. The series is structurally front-loaded, so every chronological split faces the same fork.

nodes.label: The Validation Fold Is the Omicron Peak
nodes.norm_label: the validation fold is the omicron peak
nodes.rationale: Val runs at 2.83x both other folds and requires extrapolation, and two mechanisms key off it: early stopping selects on it and the bias correction is fitted on it, then applied to a test fold at a sixth of the scale.

nodes.label: bundles.py - one interface over five bundles
nodes.norm_label: bundles.py - one interface over five bundles
nodes.rationale: The whole reason Phase 3 does not drown in special cases. It absorbs three measured divergences in one place so no model, metric or experiment file ever branches on disease: influenza ships split integers and no mask arrays while dengue and Ebola ship masks; Ebola has five channels where the others have four; and meta['node_country'] is absent for influenza, so a synthesised group map keeps score.py's country-macro degenerating to the node mean rather than raising KeyError. Do not patch the .npz.

nodes.label: DiseaseTensors.transfer_view()
nodes.rationale: Returns exactly the core block so the shared encoder cannot accidentally see an extended channel - the disease-agnosticism guarantee enforced structurally rather than by discipline.

nodes.label: Node-level-mean variance diagnostic and the dengue discrepancy
nodes.norm_label: node-level-mean variance diagnostic and the dengue discrepancy
nodes.rationale: COVID's cross-node level gradient (0.0090) is 7x flatter than influenza's on the same 49 nodes, so the spatial channel has even less to propagate. Two numbers are in circulation for dengue - 0.948 versus 0.0234 - and japan and us-states match exactly, so the method agrees everywhere except dengue; the likely cause is the denominator (a node mean over all T is crushed toward zero at 78 per cent exact zeros, a mean over observed cells only is not). Both are defensible, they are different statistics, and neither should be quoted until it is pinned down.

nodes.label: The windowing contract (w=20, h in {3,5,10,15}, direct multi-horizon)
nodes.norm_label: the windowing contract (w=20, h in {3,5,10,15}, direct multi-horizon)
nodes.rationale: An example is an origin t, not a node - the graph is consumed whole. An example's phase is decided by where its target lands, never by its input window. State this in the methods, because when scoring a test-phase target the input window legitimately contains test-period observations: that is what forecasting from a live surveillance stream means, and leakage-safety comes from elsewhere - the scaler saw only training cells and no input at or beyond t+h is ever read.

nodes.label: Day-11 close-out readings that gate Day 12
nodes.norm_label: day-11 close-out readings that gate day 12
nodes.rationale: Both are readings of Day 11's own output rather than new work: the Ebola support-origin count from the per-phase printout, which is the go/no-go on the Week-4 design, and the node-level-mean variance of X[:,:,0] per dataset, without which Task 12.6's ablation cannot be interpreted. Origin counts before phase filtering must match the guide exactly (dengue 1,375, us-regions 751, us-states 326, japan 314); that agreement is the check that the windowing contract was implemented as written.

nodes.label: Core 4-channel transfer-safe feature block
nodes.rationale: incidence_norm, sin_doy, cos_doy, obs_mask. Concatenating channels that are all-zero for some diseases injects a spurious 'this-disease-has-no-climate' signal the encoder can latch onto, quietly making the model disease-aware - the opposite of the claim.

nodes.label: DiseaseTensors bundle schema
nodes.rationale: The architecture is disease-agnostic because the input is disease-agnostic: X, A_geo, A_mob, C, M, y and meta. Disease-specific facts live only in meta and in optional extended channels, never in tensor shapes or core channels. Diseases share neither node set nor time grid, and are not required to - the framework transfers representations, not indices.

nodes.label: Extended single-disease channels (deaths_norm, logpop_norm, climate)
nodes.rationale: Available to a single-disease model and withheld from the shared one; presence/absence of a channel is itself a disease tell.

nodes.label: incidence_norm = log1p then per-node z-score
nodes.rationale: Counts are heavily right-skewed and vary orders of magnitude across nodes and diseases. Incidence is raw counts, not a per-capita rate (D10). Stats are fit on the training split only; a node with a constant training window takes its country's pooled training statistics rather than sd:=1, so it is never left un-normalised while its neighbours are standardised. Imputed steps are set to 0 in normalised space (the per-node mean), a neutral fill, not the transform of a raw zero.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable normalisation and leakage rules
nodes.rationale: Chronological splits only, no shuffling; scaler fit on observed train cells only; Ebola scaler fit on the support calendar prefix pooled per disease; graph structure is static geography or learned on train only; no future-derived features.

nodes.label: Window normalisation dropped - the released scaler is already per-node
nodes.norm_label: window normalisation dropped - the released scaler is already per-node
nodes.rationale: fit_scalers_masked returns mean/std of shape [N], so X[:,:,0] arrives at the trunk already log1p + per-node z-scored; adding a RevIN-style window norm would double-normalise, distort the sin/cos channels' relative amplitude, and collide with the per-origin refit. It resolves the earlier concern in an unexpected direction: cross-node magnitude is already gone, and gone by necessity - node-level magnitude is a proxy for population, hence geography, hence disease identity, which C1 forbids. The spatial channel therefore transports phase and shape co-movement, not magnitude gradients: real signal, since wave propagation is a timing phenomenon, but a narrower claim the manuscript must make. Only the node-level-mean variance diagnostic is retained.

nodes.label: Scope the spatial claim to timing, not magnitude (§0.9)
nodes.norm_label: scope the spatial claim to timing, not magnitude (§0.9)
nodes.rationale: Per-node standardisation removes cross-node level differences, so the graph layers cannot propagate 'my neighbour has more cases than I do'; what survives is phase and shape co-movement - does my neighbour turn upward when I do. Epidemic wave propagation is a timing phenomenon, so this is real signal, but the manuscript must say which signal it is. This is not a defect to fix: cross-node magnitude is a proxy for population and therefore for geography and therefore for disease identity, so the per-node scaler is a consequence of the disease-agnosticism constraint rather than an oversight. State the trade-off explicitly, because a reviewer who spots it unaided will assume it was accidental.

nodes.label: Static covariates C deferred (decision D20)
nodes.rationale: Ships as a flagged [N,3] placeholder. Keeping C to shapefile-derived fields by default avoids silently introducing an un-provenanced covariate into a publication.

nodes.label: obs_mask as a core channel (decision D15)
nodes.norm_label: obs_mask as a core channel (decision d15)
nodes.rationale: Lets the shared encoder distinguish real observations from filled gaps. Constant-1 for fully-observed diseases (harmless) and informative for Ebola.

nodes.label: Four isolated influenza nodes (Alaska, Hawaii, Hokkaido, Okinawa)
nodes.norm_label: four isolated influenza nodes (alaska, hawaii, hokkaido, okinawa)
nodes.rationale: Zeroing the diagonal exposed what the self-loops concealed: four nodes whose only entry was the self-loop. The isolation is inherited from the shipped graph, not introduced. They are deliberately not patched with a nearest-neighbour edge, although the builder does exactly that for dengue and Ebola, because inventing an edge absent from the shipped graph would destroy the exact comparability that is the sole reason for reusing it. They become non-degenerate only through the encoder's uniform addition of the identity - which is why that addition is a hard constraint on the model.

nodes.label: Rolling-origin backtest scaffold
nodes.rationale: Origins are fixed at build time although the backtest runs later, deliberately: deferred, the instruction to refit at each origin is exactly the step that becomes 'fit once and reuse', which leaks the test distribution into all five origins at once. Only cut points are stored - materialising dengue's masks would cost hundreds of megabytes to encode what one integer implies. Grouping mirrors the headline split, and Ebola has no rolling origins because expanding the training window beyond support is precisely the leakage the few-shot design forbids.

nodes.label: The three coded constraints carried into the modelling phase
nodes.norm_label: the three coded constraints carried into the modelling phase
nodes.rationale: Add the identity before any degree normalisation, or the four isolated influenza nodes divide by zero; keep static covariates out of the shared encoder, since geography identifies the disease; refit the scaler at every rolling origin, since the released scaler belongs to the headline split and has seen data beyond every origin. These are properties of the datasets that cannot be enforced from within them.

nodes.label: Three obligations the datasets place on the model
nodes.norm_label: three obligations the datasets place on the model
nodes.rationale: Add the identity before degree normalisation; keep static covariates out of the shared encoder; refit the scaler at each rolling origin. These are properties of the datasets that cannot be enforced from within them.

nodes.label: SpatialMixer - inductive, mask-aware message passing
nodes.rationale: Self-loop before normalisation (never invert D from A alone - four influenza nodes have degree 0 and will produce NaN); aggregation renormalised over observed neighbours only, because Ebola reporting is sparse and smoothing over unobserved neighbours propagates reporting artefacts as epidemiological signal; GraphSAGE-style separate self and neighbour weights, both d x d with no N anywhere. A node with no observed neighbours falls back to its self-loop, which the identity guarantees exists.

nodes.label: The eight ablations, each isolating one claim
nodes.norm_label: the eight ablations, each isolating one claim
nodes.rationale: Transfer vs single-disease, meta-learning vs joint training, uniform vs country-balanced sampling, disease-uniform vs proportional, the epi-informed penalty, constant nodes in vs out, core-4 vs extended channels, and the Ebola support window. Only the support-window ablation touches Ebola, and it is a parameter variation declared in advance rather than a second bite at the query set. The core-4 ablation quantifies the price of the framework's central constraint: if withholding deaths_norm and C costs little the disease-agnosticism argument gets much stronger, and if it costs a lot that is an honest limitation a reviewer will respect being measured.

nodes.label: MepoGNN - mobility-driven variant out of scope
nodes.norm_label: mepognn - mobility-driven variant out of scope
nodes.rationale: All three of its source files reference commuting/OD data and A_mob is None for every disease, so the Dynamic variant cannot run on our data. Run the adaptive/learned-graph variant if the repo exposes one and disclose that the mobility-driven variant is out of scope for want of an OD matrix - a property of our data, not a failure of the model, and it must be stated that way.

nodes.label: Refitting the scaler means rebuilding the input channel, not just the target
nodes.norm_label: refitting the scaler means rebuilding the input channel, not just the target
nodes.rationale: The sharpest trap in the phase and stated nowhere in the Phase-2 documents, because it only arises once you train. y == X[:,:,0] exactly in every bundle - both are inc_norm, written twice by _finalise. Refitting for y and leaving X[:,:,0] on the headline scaler leaks the test distribution into the model's inputs while every gate stays green, because the leakage suite runs at build time on the released bundles and cannot see what the trainer does at origin k. Write one function returning (X, y, scaler) and never touch the two separately.

nodes.label: Loss in model space, metrics in count space - asserted
nodes.norm_label: loss in model space, metrics in count space - asserted
nodes.rationale: Pinball loss is computed in log1p+z space where targets are roughly unit-scale, and all metrics after expm1. Both facts are easy to state and easy to get backwards under the per-origin refit, so guard them with an assertion on target magnitude plus a scaler round-trip test to 1e-5. Mis-ordering the two transforms is the single easiest silent bug in the trainer and it is invisible in the loss curve.

nodes.label: Disease-agnosticism reduces to one data-layer rule
nodes.norm_label: disease-agnosticism reduces to one data-layer rule
nodes.rationale: Only the core transfer-safe channels reach the shared encoder. Three exclusions, each a correctness property: the Ebola deaths channel exists for one disease only, so presence or absence alone discloses identity; the static covariates place the diseases in disjoint geography, so a raw centroid identifies the disease outright; and mismatched self-loop conventions would give influenza twice the self-weight of dengue. The earlier reason for excluding covariates - asymmetric availability - was incomplete: all three diseases now carry populated covariates and the constraint still stands, because disjoint geography is intrinsic to what the covariates are. To be shared they would have to be made geography-free.

nodes.label: Mobility adjacency declined for every disease
nodes.norm_label: mobility adjacency declined for every disease
nodes.rationale: A real commuting matrix exists for Japan and is tempting, but no equivalent exists for dengue or Ebola, so attaching it to Japan alone would reintroduce exactly the cross-disease asymmetry that zeroing the adjacency diagonal removes. Its own node ordering is also undocumented.

nodes.label: Influenza adjacency diagonal zeroed to match the built graphs
nodes.norm_label: influenza adjacency diagonal zeroed to match the built graphs
nodes.rationale: All three shipped adjacencies carry a self-loop on every node while dengue and Ebola do not, so under the standard renormalisation influenza nodes would get twice the self-weight of dengue nodes - a systematic structural difference from which the encoder could infer which disease it is looking at. Teaching the encoder to omit the identity for influenza alone is disease-specific special-casing, which reintroduces the same problem through another door. The operation is information-preserving: the shipped matrix is exactly recoverable by adding back the identity.

nodes.label: Decision thresholds that change the plan
nodes.norm_label: decision thresholds that change the plan
nodes.rationale: If the spatial channel adds less than 2-3 per cent over a temporal-only baseline on Ebola few-shot, demote spatial mixing to a light residual, lead with the temporal trunk, and open the multi-relational work. If dengue OOMs after all three memory fallbacks, drop to STGCN-style Chebyshev K <= 2.

nodes.label: Multi-relational spatial input deferred - single-relation is forced
nodes.norm_label: multi-relational spatial input deferred - single-relation is forced
nodes.rationale: Parallel channels over contiguity / distance-decay / k-NN with attention over relations is the principled answer to kernel mis-specification, but a distance-decay adjacency is a new artifact absent from the frozen bundles and would need a gated addition to the build plus per-graph edge-weight normalisation so absolute scale cannot act as a disease tell. Meanwhile bundles.Bundle has no A_mob field at all, so single-relation mixing is forced by data availability rather than chosen - say so explicitly in the limitations, because silence here reads as oversight.

nodes.norm_label: epignn protocol matches our pipeline exactly

nodes.norm_label: self-inflicted normalisation covariate shift on ebola

nodes.label: Pooled Scaling Helps on the Matched Panel
nodes.norm_label: pooled scaling helps on the matched panel

nodes.label: ANIL (MAML Restricted to the Adapter, Exact Second-Order)
nodes.norm_label: anil (maml restricted to the adapter, exact second-order)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for train-test consistency: the Ebola protocol is freeze trunk, fit adapter, score once, and ANIL's meta-objective is exactly that procedure differentiated, whereas full-network MAML optimises for an inner loop we never run. A small inner loop also makes the Hessian-vector product cheap enough for true second-order.

nodes.label: Episode Sampler and Inner Loop
nodes.rationale: Episodes defined below the disease level (country and rolling origin for dengue, panel and rolling origin for influenza) with support size matched to the Ebola regime, plus a smoke test asserting inner-loop-touches-adapter-only and non-zero second-order gradient to the trunk.

nodes.label: Re-Scope Options A, B and C
nodes.norm_label: re-scope options a, b and c
nodes.rationale: A extend by one week and protect everything; B hold 30 days and cut secondary work; C hold 30 days and run one meta direction. Cut arms, never seeds, because dropping 5 seeds to 3 pushes the t critical value from 2.78 to 4.30 and makes a positive finding harder to establish.

nodes.label: D13: ANIL, and the Schedule Answer Is No for the Full Scope
nodes.norm_label: d13: anil, and the schedule answer is no for the full scope
nodes.rationale: Scope is deliberately not decided here: options go to the client without a recommendation. Three corrections on record, including that the adapter is an exact affine read-out on frozen features and is 1,428 params rather than 388. The self-raised objection is that with two dev diseases, leave-one-disease-out leaves one meta-train disease, so ANIL would be trained on the non-problem.

nodes.label: D2: Meta-Learning Is Required, Not Optional
nodes.norm_label: d2: meta-learning is required, not optional
nodes.rationale: Lets the project answer whether meta-learning beats a linear probe with a number instead of an assertion.

nodes.label: Dengue-to-Influenza as the Direction to Keep
nodes.norm_label: dengue-to-influenza as the direction to keep
nodes.rationale: Episodic meta-training needs a task distribution and the meta-train side is where tasks come from: dengue gives twelve countries and 6,161 nodes, influenza gives three thin panels; the same direction also has the most headroom because influenza is where transfer fails worst.

nodes.label: FiLM Adapter Is Not a Linear Probe (later reversed)
nodes.norm_label: film adapter is not a linear probe (later reversed)
nodes.rationale: Offered as an accuracy correction to the client's framing, but subsequently measured false: with the trunk frozen the adapter is an exact affine read-out on frozen features, max deviation 0.0.

nodes.label: ProtoNet Excluded
nodes.rationale: A nearest-centroid classifier over class prototypes against a continuous multi-horizon regression target; making it apply would need a non-standard prototype-regression variant that is itself an unbudgeted research contribution.

nodes.label: Reptile Excluded
nodes.rationale: Its outer update is the difference between adapted and initial parameters, so an adapter-only inner loop leaves the trunk difference identically zero and the trunk never trains; the later corrected reason is that it carries no support/query meta-objective and so cannot give the controlled comparison the client asked for.

nodes.label: Schedule Answer: No for the Full Scope
nodes.norm_label: schedule answer: no for the full scope
nodes.rationale: The blocker is dependency order, not implementation difficulty: ANIL sits upstream of a single-shot Ebola evaluation, so it serialises Weeks 5 and 6 rather than running beside them, and meta-training replaces trunk training rather than extending it.

nodes.label: 200-Outer-Step Timing Probe
nodes.rationale: Replaces an estimated 6x-11x per-step multiplier with a measurement rather than quoting a wall-clock figure that was never measured on this stack.

nodes.label: Meta-Learning Is Required, Not Optional
nodes.rationale: What is implemented is transfer learning with a linear probe; the brief marks meta-learning REQUIRED under G2 and the encoder was chosen for cheap second-order differentiation, an argument that only pays off if it is used. Freeze-and-adapt becomes the ablation.

nodes.label: E1: Zero-Shot Loses to Persistence at Every Horizon
nodes.norm_label: e1: zero-shot loses to persistence at every horizon
nodes.rationale: High confidence, because LDO3 found transfer negative in 25 of 36 cells and Ebola is a further shift than any development fold.

nodes.label: Zero-Shot Mean-Adapter Definition
nodes.rationale: Element-wise mean of the three trained in-disease adapters applied to Ebola with no fitting; no Ebola label touched at any point.

nodes.label: Cross-Disease Transfer Is Negative (25 of 36 Cells)
nodes.norm_label: cross-disease transfer is negative (25 of 36 cells)
nodes.rationale: With the disease genuinely held out and judged by the paired origin bootstrap: 25 cells significantly worse than the single-disease ceiling, 10 within noise, 1 better. The adapted arm is the optimistic bound because the held-out disease got its entire train fold to fit the adapter.

nodes.label: Paired Bootstrap Over Time Origins (B=10,000)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds both arms from the same resampled origins so shared origin noise cancels; covers RMSE and MAE only, because PCC is not additive over origins from the stored sufficient statistics.

nodes.label: The Zero-Shot Arm Fails Everywhere
nodes.rationale: The borrowed mean adapter is behind the ceiling in 36 of 36 attributable cells, 34 significantly, and ahead in none; averaging in-disease adapters produces nothing usable on an unseen disease.

nodes.label: Three-Disease Leave-One-Disease-Out Results
nodes.rationale: Generated by ldo3_report.py from results/lodo artifacts: 3 held-out diseases x 5 seeds = 15 runs, country-macro headline, nothing averaged across datasets.

nodes.label: Where the Bootstrap Disagrees with the Seed-Paired Test
nodes.norm_label: where the bootstrap disagrees with the seed-paired test
nodes.rationale: They are two different quantities, not two measurements of one: section 2 averages per-node scores while the bootstrap pools cells before the square root, and on COVID the state-level counts span orders of magnitude. No positive COVID transfer claim is made because the arm producing positives does not survive the other test.

nodes.label: COVID Long Horizons Excluded, Not Counted as Losses
nodes.norm_label: covid long horizons excluded, not counted as losses
nodes.rationale: The COVID test fold is a flat tail on the far side of the Omicron break while selection happens on the surge, so h10 and h15 measure a fold boundary rather than transfer. Applied symmetrically: the ceiling is degraded by the same break, so no positive COVID claim is made either.

nodes.label: Every Fold Varies Graph, Geography and Node Count
nodes.norm_label: every fold varies graph, geography and node count
nodes.rationale: Three held-out diseases with one bundle for dengue, one for COVID and three for influenza is the whole cross-disease evidence base, so a negative here is not attributable to the disease change on its own; the graph-controlled COVID/influenza-US-states pair is the fold that isolates the disease.

nodes.label: Transfer Degrades Monotonically with Horizon
nodes.rationale: At h3 the transfer arm is close to parity with a model trained on the disease itself; by h10 and h15 it is uniformly and substantially worse, reaching -38% and -51%. A frozen foreign trunk carries short-range structure for a few weeks ahead and then loses it.

nodes.label: Option B: The Disease Must Be Trained On Directly
nodes.norm_label: option b: the disease must be trained on directly
nodes.rationale: The trunk does not transfer across diseases well enough to carry a held-out disease, and Ebola will have 27 labelled support cells rather than a train fold, so few-shot Ebola cannot do better than these numbers and will very likely do worse.

nodes.label: COVID Survives as a Transfer Source, Not a Target
nodes.norm_label: covid survives as a transfer source, not a target
nodes.rationale: The covid-to-influenza direction rests on the influenza ceiling, which beats every floor, so it remains publishable; the influenza-to-covid direction is the uninterpretable half, and the blocker as written should be re-scoped by horizon because at h10/h15 no model can clear it.

nodes.label: configs/frozen_ebola_protocol.json (the Day-19 freeze)
nodes.rationale: Read-only after writing: encoder hyperparameters, adapter definition, inner steps, inner LR, support scheme, seeds and a hash of the code that produced them. Everything after this point reads the file and nothing writes it. Record why each value was chosen and which development fold chose it, because that paragraph is a manuscript section and is much harder to reconstruct in Week 6 than to write on the day.

nodes.label: run_ebola_once.py and the query receipt
nodes.rationale: Writes results/ebola_query_receipt.json with the frozen-config hash, the code hash, a timestamp and the scores, and refuses to run if that file exists; re-running requires an explicit flag and appends a new receipt rather than overwriting. The receipt is the audit trail that the query set was scored once, and it is what you show a reviewer who asks.

nodes.label: Calendar-prefix few-shot support protocol
nodes.rationale: Every observed cell on or before a fixed cutoff is support; every later observed cell is query. It replaced a per-district scheme (first two observed weeks of each district) that was not calendar-causal: support cells spanned 2014-04-12 to 2015-02-14 and 1,004 of 1,178 query cells (85 per cent) lay earlier in calendar time than the last support cell, so the pooled scaler normalising an early cell was a function of another district's peak-epidemic magnitudes. That defect was invisible to the suite structurally, because the old check defined the support mask as the legitimate fit set - the assumption under attack. Under the Phase-2 cutoff 2014-05-24: 27 support cells across 9 districts, 1,272 query cells, and 52 of 61 districts pure zero-shot, which is the genuine emerging-outbreak regime rather than a defect.

nodes.label: Two frozen Ebola support-length arms (L12 primary, L20 secondary)
nodes.norm_label: two frozen ebola support-length arms (l12 primary, l20 secondary)
nodes.rationale: The Phase-2 cutoff yields zero adaptation pairs at h10 and h15, so the client (D16) chose to run both arms pre-registered, frozen and hashed before either is scored: cutoff 2014-06-28 (59 support cells, 18 districts, 0 pairs at h15) and 2014-08-23 (113 cells, 36 districts, 54 pairs at h15). The query counts are identical under both arms because a full-window query target sits at column 22 and support reaches at most column 20, so the arms differ only in labelled adaptation data, never in what is evaluated - asserted by freeze_ebola_arms.py rather than assumed. The L labels are 0-based indices of the last support column, off by one against the column counts; the cutoff date is the operative definition.

nodes.label: Scored vs reachable pairs (pre-registration amendment A1)
nodes.norm_label: scored vs reachable pairs (pre-registration amendment a1)
nodes.rationale: Reachable counts per-horizon origins, so h3 reaches origin 48 and h15 only 36; scored uses one common origin set for every horizon, t in [19,36], which is what bundles.origins() returns and therefore what score_predictions evaluates. Horizons are comparable to each other only if read at the same origins, so the common set is the right protocol - and quoting the reachable figures as the evaluation size overstates h3/h5/h10 by 34 to 52 per cent. Found by reading the scoring path before the run rather than after it.

nodes.label: C8 - Ebola never enters model selection
nodes.norm_label: c8 - ebola never enters model selection
nodes.rationale: All encoder hyperparameters are selected on development validation folds and adaptation settings by leave-one-development-disease-out, then frozen; Ebola's query set is scored once with a fixed number of adaptation steps and no early stopping on query, and carries no validation split by design. Any code path that reads an Ebola metric before the final run is a correctness bug, and test_ebola_never_in_selection exists to catch it.

nodes.label: BLOCKER - Ebola has zero support origins under the frozen protocol
nodes.norm_label: blocker - ebola has zero support origins under the frozen protocol
nodes.rationale: Support is a calendar prefix through 2014-05-24 = week index 7, so all 27 support cells lie in t in [0,7]; origins() requires t >= 19 and t+15 <= 51, so the earliest target cell is t+3 = 22. The sets are disjoint and the inner loop has nothing to supervise on. Resolution: separate the adaptation protocol from the evaluation protocol, since only the latter is frozen - left-pad short windows for adaptation only, accept that h=10 and h=15 admit no support target under any windowing choice, and reframe the headline as zero-shot with light short-horizon adaptation, which is both the honest framing and the stronger claim given 52 of 61 districts are zero-shot regardless.

nodes.label: Rehearse the Ebola path without scoring it (Day 20)
nodes.norm_label: rehearse the ebola path without scoring it (day 20)
nodes.rationale: Find every bug in the Ebola path while the query set is still sealed: run adaptation on the support cells, produce query-shaped predictions, assert shapes, absence of NaN and the pooled-support scaler, and compute no metric. Verify that the 52 districts with no support cell - the paper's central regime - all receive predictions, because a bug there surfacing on Day 21 costs the single evaluation.

nodes.label: The k-shot sweep on calendar-prefix surrogates
nodes.norm_label: the k-shot sweep on calendar-prefix surrogates
nodes.rationale: Treat each held-out development disease as a surrogate emerging pathogen under the same calendar-prefix support construction, sweeping k, inner steps and inner LR; the curve is the headline figure for G3 - the quantitative statement of how little data the framework needs. The surrogate must be built the way Ebola's was, as a calendar prefix rather than the first k observed weeks per node, because selecting adaptation settings on an acausally-built surrogate would tune for a regime Ebola does not present.

nodes.label: [CONFIRM-P7] - split the adaptation protocol from the evaluation protocol
nodes.norm_label: [confirm-p7] - split the adaptation protocol from the evaluation protocol
nodes.rationale: The most consequential of the confirm items, because it changes what Week 5 can claim. Only the evaluation protocol is frozen, so left-padding short windows for adaptation only is legitimate and needs no bundle change; h=10 and h=15 admit no support target under any windowing choice and are structurally zero-shot; the Week-5 headline is reframed as zero-shot with light short-horizon adaptation. The alternative - re-cutting the Ebola support definition - changes a frozen bundle and invalidates the Phase-2 gate suite. It is also the one Week-3 item that can silently invalidate a whole Week-4 day, since the k-shot sweep and the Day-19 freeze both assume support origins exist.

nodes.label: Ebola's query set is scored exactly once, and process is the only protection
nodes.norm_label: ebola's query set is scored exactly once, and process is the only protection
nodes.rationale: Every hyperparameter is selected on the development diseases and then frozen. There is no technical control preventing a peek - 1,272 query cells sit in a file you can load at any moment - so until the receipt exists the rule is behavioural: ebola.npz's query mask does not enter any loop that chooses anything, not for a sanity check, not for a shape assertion, not 'just to see'.

nodes.label: Ebola enters no loop that chooses anything in Week 3
nodes.norm_label: ebola enters no loop that chooses anything in week 3
nodes.rationale: The control that makes a second run visible is not built until Day 20, so the Week-3 rule is behavioural and absolute. Everything needed to size the design against Ebola is already in the guide - 61 nodes, 52 weeks, 27 support cells, 9 of 61 districts carrying support - so there is no reason to open the file.

nodes.label: C2 - no shared-trunk parameter may have a dimension equal to N
nodes.norm_label: c2 - no shared-trunk parameter may have a dimension equal to n
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing constraint: it is what makes the transfer claim mechanically true rather than asserted. Implemented as a runtime assertion over named_parameters() against the node counts {10, 47, 49, 61, 7165}.

nodes.label: TemporalEncoder - dilated causal TCN, shared and inductive
nodes.norm_label: temporalencoder - dilated causal tcn, shared and inductive
nodes.rationale: The Graph-WaveNet temporal block with the adaptive-adjacency machinery removed: 5 layers, dilations [1,2,4,8,16], kernel 2, gated activation, residual and skip connections, d=64. Nodes go into the batch dimension, so the module is node-count-agnostic for free and satisfies C2 trivially. Chosen over a recurrent trunk partly because Week-4 MAML inner loops backpropagate through the adaptation step, and doing that through a recurrent net over 20 timesteps is where memory and wall-clock die.

nodes.label: Factorised inductive temporal-then-spatial encoder (Option 1)
nodes.rationale: A strictly inductive temporal-per-node encoder followed by gated inductive spatial message passing, with a direct multi-horizon head and a light per-disease adaptation surface. Factorisation is preferred over STGCN-style interleaving because the diseases do not share a transmission kernel - dengue spreads over short-range vector-suitable geography, Ebola by distance- and population-weighted human movement - so a mis-specified graph is expected, not exceptional. Factorisation quarantines that error in one gated channel; interleaving lets it contaminate the temporal representation at every block.

nodes.label: Adaptation surface - FiLM modulation plus head (~388 params)
nodes.norm_label: adaptation surface - film modulation plus head (~388 params)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately tiny: Ebola's 27 support cells yield very few usable adaptation origins and none at h=10/15, so a few hundred parameters can move but cannot possibly discover a transmission topology. The burden of learning structure sits in pre-training and graph construction, never in the inner loop. Build the shared_params()/adaptation_params() split now so Week 4 is a training-loop change only.

nodes.label: Memory budget and fallback order on the 12 GB card
nodes.norm_label: memory budget and fallback order on the 12 gb card
nodes.rationale: Full-graph forward is comfortable at [7165, 20, 64] fp32 (~37 MB per activation) provided A stays a sparse COO tensor; densifying a 7,165^2 matrix is 205 MB fp32 alone and will end the run. Fallbacks in order: gradient checkpointing on the TCN, neighbour sampling over dengue only, then d=48.

nodes.label: Receptive-field assertion (RF >= lookback)
nodes.rationale: An earlier draft specified kernel 2 with dilations [1,2,4], which is RF 8 - it would have silently ignored 60 per cent of the lookback window while training, converging and producing plausible numbers. Asserted at construction as rf = 1 + sum((k-1)*d), with a paired negative control requiring [1,2,4] to fail.

nodes.label: First-order MAML (Reptile-style) over diseases as tasks
nodes.norm_label: first-order maml (reptile-style) over diseases as tasks
nodes.rationale: Full second-order MAML roughly triples memory for a benefit usually small at this scale, and first-order variants keep the 7,165-node dengue graph inside 12 GB. The inner loop adapts only the per-disease adapter, matching exactly what will be adapted on Ebola, with plain multi-task joint training as the meta-learning-free control. Adversarial disease-discrimination was rejected because the discriminator can trivially separate diseases by graph size, so it would learn to erase useful signal.

nodes.label: MTGNN (non-epidemic control row)
nodes.rationale: Kept as the control row because it establishes what a general ST-GNN achieves without epidemic structure.

nodes.label: Correction B - the temporal stack's receptive field is 4, not 20
nodes.norm_label: correction b - the temporal stack's receptive field is 4, not 20
nodes.rationale: Revision 1's '2 temporal blocks (dilations 1,2)' gives RF = 4, so the encoder would see 4 of the 20 lookback timesteps and ignore the other 16. It would still train, still converge and still produce plausible numbers; the only symptom would be a baffling ablation in which w=20 and w=4 perform identically, and by then Weeks 4-5 would be built on it. Use kernel 2 with dilations (1,2,4,8,16) for RF 32, assert at construction, and pair the assertion with a negative control in which (1,2) must fail. A blocking defect for Day 12.

nodes.label: PEMS (ICLR 2024) and CAPE (2025) - the closest transferable prior art
nodes.norm_label: pems (iclr 2024) and cape (2025) - the closest transferable prior art
nodes.rationale: They prove cross-disease pre-training works but are purely temporal with no spatial encoder. An inductive spatial channel over a shared temporal trunk is precisely the unoccupied cell, and it is the contribution.

nodes.label: Node-indexed parameters eliminate most of the state of the art
nodes.norm_label: node-indexed parameters eliminate most of the state of the art
nodes.rationale: One set of shared weights must run unchanged over graphs of 10/47/49/61/7,165 nodes across disjoint geographies. Graph WaveNet, MTGNN and AGCRN all carry a learned node-embedding dictionary E in R^{Nxd}, and EpiGNN a learnable W^s in R^{NxN} - parameters indexed by node, sized by N, therefore both untransferable and a direct disease tell. Cola-GNN, STAN, MepoGNN and CausalGNN are single-disease by construction or bake in compartmental parameters that violate disease-agnosticism if placed in the trunk.

nodes.label: GTR and RAGL checked against the constraints and rejected
nodes.norm_label: gtr and ragl checked against the constraints and rejected
nodes.rationale: GTR computes full self-attention over all N nodes, a dense NxN matrix that at dengue's N=7,165 reopens the ~205 MB memory liability already ruled out for A_geo. RAGL's adaptive edge gate uses W_s in R^{NxN}, a learnable parameter matrix sized to one dataset's node count, so it cannot be a shared-weight component of a trunk running across N = 10, 47, 49, 61 and 7,165 - porting it as published would silently break the disease-agnostic-trunk constraint, the same class of silent failure as an unrefit input channel. A constraint-clean version of RAGL's idea (a small N-independent bilinear gate over existing edges) is deferred to Week 6 as an ablation candidate.

nodes.rationale: The client's response to the Week 3 summary: direction call, fold fix, reporting standards and the rest of the work order.

nodes.rationale: Under the corrected disease-level fold, 12 of 16 RMSE cells are significantly negative, 4 within noise and 0 positive; the three largest earlier gains were influenza panels with influenza still in training, and holding the transfer number fixed while varying only the reference reproduces all three client arithmetic complaints to the decimal. The paper's central claim as previously framed is not supported by the project's own corrected experiment.

nodes.label: D1: Transfer, With the Folds Fixed First
nodes.norm_label: d1: transfer, with the folds fixed first
nodes.rationale: Leave-one-out over four datasets holds out a population, not a disease, and the two strongest folds are the ones with the most influenza leakage; spending seeds on the wrong fold structure buys nothing.

nodes.label: D5: Transfer-Table Reference and Dispersion
nodes.rationale: train/lodo.py::_report compared LODO to seed 42's own single run while the docs quoted 5-seed means, and seed 42 is an unusually bad single-disease seed, so a seed-matched reference flattered LODO. The formula was correct, the reference was not; both references are now reported with a paired origin bootstrap as the verdict.

nodes.norm_label: hold the five seeds until the folds are fixed
nodes.rationale: Three of four datasets are influenza, so holding out flu-Japan still leaves flu-US-regions and flu-US-states in training; spending five seeds on the wrong fold structure buys nothing because the compute is gone and the paper still lacks its number.

nodes.rationale: The superseded table compared LODO to seed 42's own single run while every other table quoted 5-seed means; against the right reference the only cell that is both origin-stable and clears the seed-noise screen as positive is japan h3, and dengue, the only genuinely held-out disease, is negative at every horizon.

nodes.label: Ebola signal-confirmation audit (ebola_audit.py)
nodes.rationale: Data scarcity was the project's principal risk, so usable signal had to be confirmed before the few-shot design could rest on it. Read-only, escalates on any drift from the recorded figures, and re-asserts every count on each run - so a change in the source file's contents fails loudly rather than quietly shifting the reported numbers. 64 clean district series, mean 27.1 observed weeks, 1,299 observed cells.

nodes.label: Risk: Ebola data scarcity
nodes.rationale: Mitigated by confirming usable signal in the Week-2 audit before the few-shot design is allowed to rest on it.

nodes.label: Generalizable Spatio-Temporal Framework for EID Forecasting
nodes.norm_label: generalizable spatio-temporal framework for eid forecasting
nodes.rationale: Disease-agnostic by construction because recent SOTA is single-disease or stays inside one disease family and several papers explicitly flag cross-disease transferability as open future work; the unoccupied gap is the intersection (disease-agnostic x transferable x few-shot x calibrated).

nodes.label: G1 - Disease-agnostic spatio-temporal architecture
nodes.rationale: Operating on a standardised input schema is what makes the architecture disease-agnostic; the input, not the model, carries the guarantee.

nodes.label: G3 - Few-shot generalisation to data-scarce Ebola
nodes.norm_label: g3 - few-shot generalisation to data-scarce ebola
nodes.rationale: Ebola is treated as a few-shot test precisely because the data is thin; scarcity is the design premise rather than an obstacle.

nodes.label: GradientSHAP explainability, scoped tightly
nodes.rationale: KernelSHAP is prohibitively expensive on a 7,165-node graph and attention weights are neither SHAP nor faithful. Global attributions per channel and per lag have a checkable expected ordering - recent lags and incidence dominate, with the seasonality channels weighing more on influenza than on Ebola, since a 52-week outbreak has no seasonal cycle to learn - and if that ordering does not appear, distrust the attribution before distrusting the epidemiology. Spatial neighbour attribution by edge ablation answers the question the paper poses: where does a forecast for a district we have never observed actually come from?

nodes.label: Epidemiology-informed inductive bias (metapopulation / physics-informed loss)
nodes.rationale: Tagged SUGGESTION not REQUIRED: it buys data efficiency and generalisation but mechanistic hybridisation is not one of the four axes of the identified research gap, so it dilutes a contribution that is already precisely located.

nodes.label: Four design pillars (none disease-specific)
nodes.rationale: Encoder, epi-informed inductive bias, transferable representation learning with few-shot adaptation, and calibrated uncertainty; each is chosen so that nothing in the methodology is specialised to one disease.

nodes.label: Out of scope: risk stratification and intervention ranking
nodes.norm_label: out of scope: risk stratification and intervention ranking

nodes.label: bias_c mean-vs-median count-space correction
nodes.rationale: Measures the gap between the count-space mean (what RMSE rewards) and the count-space median (what the quantile head predicts). COVID's node-median gap is 3.03x against influenza's 1.74x on the identical nodes, so COVID should fit a visibly larger bias_c - but it is fitted on val, which owns Omicron, so it will over-correct. This is the first bundle where the val-only fitting rule is actively harmful rather than merely conservative; the defensible alternative is fitting COVID's bias_c on train and saying so.

nodes.label: encoder_mc arm matters most on COVID
nodes.norm_label: encoder_mc arm matters most on covid
nodes.rationale: COVID has the largest mean/median gap of any panel (3.03x), so the arm that corrects for it has the most to do here.

nodes.label: Encoder-view Wasserstein distance matrix (z-space)
nodes.rationale: Pairwise distributional distance between bundles as the shared encoder sees them; dengue is the most distant panel from everything else (0.64-0.90) while the three influenza panels cluster tightly (0.23-0.39), and covid-ebola is the largest distance in the matrix at 0.804.

nodes.label: Quantile head with pinball loss, superseding the point head
nodes.norm_label: quantile head with pinball loss, superseding the point head
nodes.rationale: invert_scaler is expm1(sigma*z + mu), strictly monotone, and quantiles are equivariant under monotone transforms, so a predicted 95th percentile in model space inverts to exactly the 95th percentile in count space. A Gaussian's mean and variance do not survive expm1 - the inverted distribution is log-normal and the closed-form CRPS no longer applies. Since Week 5 needs CRPS, PICP and interval width in count space, the quantile head makes every uncertainty number exact by construction. Linear(d -> |H| x |Q|) emits all four horizons x five levels in one pass; the median is the point forecast.

nodes.label: G4 - Calibrated uncertainty on all forecasts
nodes.norm_label: g4 - calibrated uncertainty on all forecasts

nodes.label: Adaptive conformal inference (ACI) for calibrated intervals
nodes.norm_label: adaptive conformal inference (aci) for calibrated intervals
nodes.rationale: Maintain alpha_t online along the calendar with alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma(alpha - err_t) and emit the alpha_t-level interval from the quantile head. Chosen precisely because it needs no held-out calibration set, which Ebola does not have. Cross-check against split conformal on the development diseases, which do have a validation fold: agreement there is the evidence the implementation is correct before it is trusted where no cross-check exists. Calibration must be reported per horizon, since coverage that holds at h=3 and collapses at h=15 is the normal failure mode and is a finding, not something to average away.

nodes.label: Conformal prediction as the recommended UQ route
nodes.norm_label: conformal prediction as the recommended uq route
nodes.rationale: Model-agnostic and post-hoc, so UQ stays out of the Week-3 model build; a Bayesian alternative would move UQ into the model build and must therefore be decided before Week 3.

nodes.label: Uncertainty under distribution shift and the zero-shot districts
nodes.norm_label: uncertainty under distribution shift and the zero-shot districts
nodes.rationale: The interesting calibration question is not whether PICP is 90 per cent on dengue's test fold but whether coverage survives on a held-out disease and, within it, on the 52 zero-shot districts. Widening intervals there is the correct behaviour and should be shown, not apologised for - a model that knows it is uncertain where it has no data is the calibration claim.

nodes.label: Dengue block-diagonal graph - a known mis-specification
nodes.norm_label: dengue block-diagonal graph - a known mis-specification
nodes.rationale: 7,165 nodes, 20,468 undirected edges, mean degree 5.71, zero cross-border edges. The construction was justified on the premise that the dengue countries are not adjacent, and that premise is marked False: Brazil borders Colombia, Peru, Bolivia and Argentina, so the block-diagonal build severs real transmission corridors including Leticia-Tabatinga and the Triple Frontier. Defensible only as a deliberate simplification, and recorded as such rather than as a geographic fact. Contiguity is also an induced subgraph, so degree is a property of coverage as well as of geography.

nodes.label: Ebola graph is deliberately not block-diagonal
nodes.norm_label: ebola graph is deliberately not block-diagonal
nodes.rationale: Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone are physically contiguous and 2014 was a single outbreak spreading across them, so the dengue rationale does not transfer: the Gueckedou-Lofa-Kailahun tri-border area is the defining transmission pathway, and a block-diagonal graph would sever exactly the edges carrying the epidemiological signal. That would be a modelling error, not a convention choice. 61 nodes, 146 edges, 21 cross-border edges, all three tri-border edges asserted on every build.

nodes.label: The gate x augmentation 2x2 (the primary ablation)
nodes.norm_label: the gate x augmentation 2x2 (the primary ablation)
nodes.rationale: Augmentation and the gate are in direct tension and can cancel: under aggressive augmentation the optimal policy is g -> 0 everywhere, because the encoder learns the graph is unreliable precisely because you made it unreliable, and the paper's two novel components neutralise each other. Two separate one-way ablations cannot distinguish 'augmentation helps' from 'augmentation suppressed the gate and the temporal trunk carried the result', so the primary table is {gate on, g=0} x {topo-aug none, edge_drop} at 5 seeds per cell.

nodes.label: The learned spatial gate (a contribution, not plumbing)
nodes.norm_label: the learned spatial gate (a contribution, not plumbing)
nodes.rationale: g = sigmoid(MLP(h)), a per-node scalar from a small d -> d/4 -> 1 MLP, so data-dependent, inductive and C2-clean; h_out = (1-g)h + g*h_spatial. Three reasons: graceful degradation, since if geography is uninformative g -> 0 and the encoder collapses to the graph-free forecaster so the spatial channel can only help; defect mitigation, since the dengue topology is known mis-specified; and reportability - but not as raw g, which is not scale-free because a model can reach identical effective mixing with g=0.2 and a large-norm spatial branch. Report the norm-normalised spatial contribution instead and keep raw g as a debug metric.

nodes.label: Topology-robust pre-training (edge dropout, rewiring)
nodes.rationale: Perturb the graph every origin so the encoder never learns to trust a single topology; it is explicitly trained for graph mis-specification, which is the Ebola condition and, per the audit, the dengue condition too. Never perturb at evaluation. Anneal p_drop linearly 0 -> 0.3 over the first 30 per cent of training so the gate learns on a trustworthy graph before robustness pressure arrives.

nodes.label: [CONFIRM-P8] - learned spatial gate, default on
nodes.rationale: Default chosen so the encoder nests the graph-free model and the spatial channel cannot degrade Week-5 transfer. Paired with a Day-12 gate: forcing g=0 must reproduce the temporal-only model exactly.

nodes.label: [CONFIRM-P9] - annealed edge dropout with the 2x2 reported
nodes.norm_label: [confirm-p9] - annealed edge dropout with the 2x2 reported
nodes.rationale: Default on because one training graph is already known mis-specified and the encoder will be asked in Week 5 to run on a graph built by a different process for a disease with a different transmission kernel. Annealing is required so the gate learns on a trustworthy graph first, and the 2x2 is required because two one-way ablations cannot separate 'augmentation helps' from 'augmentation suppressed the gate'.

nodes.norm_label: queen contiguity with k-nearest-centroid island fallback
nodes.rationale: GNN message passing degenerates on isolated nodes, so the k=4 fallback is a correctness fix rather than a tuning knob. Raw adjacency is stored so each model applies its own self-loop and normalisation convention.
